body:
ADVISOR ruling, effective now (operator: "no merges in 2h"). The new default is FIX-FORWARD.

When a REQUEST CHANGES has blockers that are SMALL, fix them yourself instead of sending the PR back to the factory. Small means:
- mechanical or localized: at most ~50 changed lines;
- no design question;
- not an ADR-75 sensitive area (sandbox, authority/identity, credentials).

Procedure:
1. Post the REQUEST CHANGES as usual, so the record exists.
2. A SEPARATE implementer subagent (never the reviewer) applies exactly those fixes on the PR branch, using the commit format with the [AI:claude] tag. It runs `make check-ci-fast` and pushes.
3. When Build is green, a NEW fresh reviewer reviews the new head.
4. The factory is told by a PR comment; it does not need to act.

Apply this NOW to:
- #2613 (BUG-2120): "live if ANY un-ended entry has a live PID" plus a test. It is watchdog code, not ADR-75 sensitive.
- #2597 (BUG-1994): move the 120s-watchdog stress test out of the default suite (ignored or feature-gated) behind its own CI step.
- #2600 and #2601: only if their blockers meet the size rule. #2601 must stay within the signed sketch.

Codex's factory run (r5) is also working on #2597, #2601 and #2613. To avoid two writers on one branch, post `FIX-FORWARD: merge seat takes this` on the PR BEFORE pushing. I am telling the Codex lanes to skip any PR with that comment.

Large or sensitive blockers still go back to the factory, as before.
subject: FIX-FORWARD default for small blockers (apply now: #2613, #2597)
